references.text: God's promise to Jacob that his descendants would become a great nation, now fulfilled in Egypt
God's promise to Abraham that his offspring would be as numerous as the stars in the sky and the sand on the seashore
God's promise to Abraham of countless descendants
The original promise to Abraham that he would become a great nation
A look back at how the Israelites became a great and powerful people in Egypt
The psalmist describes how God made his people very fruitful and stronger than their enemies
Stephen's speech refers to this period when the people grew and became numerous in Egypt, until a new king who did not know Joseph came to power
Theological contrast: Human fear of Israel's strength versus God's judgment on their disobedience using identical wording.
Thematic parallel about 'numerousness': Pharaoh's fear of Israel's numbers versus the prophet's comfort regarding God's superior strength.
Ironic reflection of fear: The enemy's fear of Israel's strength versus Israel's own fear of the enemy's strength.
